Basis for Intervening:
For the reasons set forth below, the Union of Concerned Scientists has interests which may be materially affected by the outcome of these proceeding, and no other parties can represent its interests.

The Union of Concerned Scientists is a national nonprofit organization founded more than 50 years ago. The Union of Concerned Scientists uses rigorous, independence science to develop solutions and advocate for a healthy, safe, and just future. An important part of the advocacy of the Union of Concerned Scientists focuses on promoting a reliable transition to a clean energy system, including advocacy for rules that will promote the development transmission necessary to move electricity from areas where clean energy is abundant to areas where demand is high. These proceedings raise issues which are important to the interests that the Union of Concerned Scientists seeks to advance. Accordingly, the Union of Concerned Scientists’ participation is in the public interest within the meaning of Commission Rule 214(b)(2)(iii), 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(2)(iii).

Pursuant to Commission Rule 214(b)(1), the Union of Concerned Scientists specifies that it seeks to intervene in these proceedings to explain how the Commission should revise Order No. 1977 in order to be more consistent with the Federal Power Act, the Commission’s trust duty to Tribes, the National Environmental Policy Act, and other federal laws and regulations, as will be specified in greater detail in a request for rehearing on Order No. 1977.

Respectfully submitted,

Lee Shaver, Senior Energy Analyst
